  60 │ def _mask_hidden_input(message: str, value: str) -> str:

  65 │     uses word-boundary lookarounds so a substring like ``"1"`` does not
  66 │     match inside ``"10"``, and ``"ent"`` does not match inside
  67 │     ``"Authentication"``. The empty string is skipped to avoid matching
  68 │     at every boundary.

  71 │     if value:
  72 │         message = re.sub(
  73 │             rf"(?<!\w){re.escape(value)}(?!\w)", _HIDDEN_INPUT_MASK, message

 418 │     to iterate over something while showing a progress bar.  It will
 419 │     either iterate over the `iterable` or `length` items (that are counted
 420 │     up).  While iteration happens, this function will print a rendered
 421 │     progress bar to the given `file` (defaults to stdout) and will attempt
 422 │     to calculate remaining time and more.  By default, this progress bar
 423 │     will not be rendered if the file is not a terminal.
 424 │ 
 425 │     The context manager creates the progress bar.  When the context
 426 │     manager is entered the progress bar is already created.  With every
 427 │     iteration over the progress bar, the iterable passed to the bar is
 428 │     advanced and the bar is updated.  When the context manager exits,
 429 │     a newline is printed and the progress bar is finalized on screen.
 430 │ 
 431 │     Note: The progress bar is currently designed for use cases where the
 432 │     total progress can be expected to take at least several seconds.
 433 │     Because of this, the ProgressBar class object won't display
 434 │     progress that is considered too fast, and progress where the time
 435 │     between steps is less than a second.
 436 │ 
 437 │     No printing must happen or the progress bar will be unintentionally
 438 │     destroyed.
 439 │ 
 440 │     Example usage::
 441 │ 
 442 │         with progressbar(items) as bar:
 443 │             for item in bar:
 444 │                 do_something_with(item)
 445 │ 
 446 │     Alternatively, if no iterable is specified, one can manually update the
 447 │     progress bar through the `update()` method instead of directly
 448 │     iterating over the progress bar.  The update method accepts the number
 449 │     of steps to increment the bar with::

 323 │ def echo_via_pager(
 324 │     text_or_generator: cabc.Iterable[str] | t.Callable[[], cabc.Iterable[str]] | str,
 325 │     color: bool | None = None,
 326 │ ) -> None:
 327 │     """This function takes a text and shows it via an environment specific
 328 │     pager on stdout.
 329 │ 
 330 │     .. versionchanged:: 3.0
 331 │        Added the `color` flag.
 332 │ 
 333 │     :param text_or_generator: the text to page, or alternatively, a
 334 │                               generator emitting the text to page.
 335 │     :param color: controls if the pager supports ANSI colors or not.  The
 336 │                   default is autodetection.
 337 │     """
 338 │ 
 339 │     if inspect.isgeneratorfunction(text_or_generator):
 340 │         i = t.cast("t.Callable[[], cabc.Iterable[str]]", text_or_generator)()

 342 │         i = [text_or_generator]
 343 │     else:
 344 │         i = iter(t.cast("cabc.Iterable[str]", text_or_generator))

 346 │     # convert every element of i to a text type if necessary
 347 │     text_generator = (el if isinstance(el, str) else str(el) for el in i)

 349 │     with get_pager_file(color=color) as pager:
 350 │         for text in itertools.chain(text_generator, "\n"):
 351 │             pager.write(text)
 352 │             # Flush after each write so a slow generator streams to the pager
 353 │             # incrementally rather than staying invisible until the pipe buffer

 399 │ def progressbar(
 400 │     iterable: cabc.Iterable[V] | None = None,
 401 │     length: int | None = None,
 402 │     label: str | None = None,
 403 │     hidden: bool = False,
 404 │     show_eta: bool = True,
 405 │     show_percent: bool | None = None,
 406 │     show_pos: bool = False,
 407 │     item_show_func: t.Callable[[V | None], str | None] | None = None,
 408 │     fill_char: str = "#",
 409 │     empty_char: str = "-",
 410 │     bar_template: str = "%(label)s  [%(bar)s]  %(info)s",
 411 │     info_sep: str = "  ",
 412 │     width: int = 36,
 413 │     file: t.TextIO | None = None,
 414 │     color: bool | None = None,
 415 │     update_min_steps: int = 1,
 416 │ ) -> ProgressBar[V]:
 417 │     """This function creates an iterable context manager that can be used
 418 │     to iterate over something while showing a progress bar.  It will
 419 │     either iterate over the `iterable` or `length` items (that are counted
 420 │     up).  While iteration happens, this function will print a rendered
 421 │     progress bar to the given `file` (defaults to stdout) and will attempt
 422 │     to calculate remaining time and more.  By default, this progress bar
 423 │     will not be rendered if the file is not a terminal.
 424 │ 
 425 │     The context manager creates the progress bar.  When the context
 426 │     manager is entered the progress bar is already created.  With every
 427 │     iteration over the progress bar, the iterable passed to the bar is
 428 │     advanced and the bar is updated.  When the context manager exits,
 429 │     a newline is printed and the progress bar is finalized on screen.
 430 │ 
 431 │     Note: The progress bar is currently designed for use cases where the
 432 │     total progress can be expected to take at least several seconds.
 433 │     Because of this, the ProgressBar class object won't display
 434 │     progress that is considered too fast, and progress where the time
 435 │     between steps is less than a second.
 436 │ 
 437 │     No printing must happen or the progress bar will be unintentionally
 438 │     destroyed.
 439 │ 
 440 │     Example usage::
 441 │ 
 442 │         with progressbar(items) as bar:
 443 │             for item in bar:
 444 │                 do_something_with(item)
 445 │ 
 446 │     Alternatively, if no iterable is specified, one can manually update the
 447 │     progress bar through the `update()` method instead of directly
 448 │     iterating over the progress bar.  The update method accepts the number
 449 │     of steps to increment the bar with::
 450 │ 
 451 │         with progressbar(length=chunks.total_bytes) as bar:
 452 │             for chunk in chunks:
 453 │                 process_chunk(chunk)
 454 │                 bar.update(chunks.bytes)
 455 │ 
 456 │     The ``update()`` method also takes an optional value specifying the
 457 │     ``current_item`` at the new position. This is useful when used
 458 │     together with ``item_show_func`` to customize the output for each
 459 │     manual step::
 460 │ 
 461 │         with click.progressbar(
 462 │             length=total_size,
 463 │             label='Unzipping archive',
 464 │             item_show_func=lambda a: a.filename
 465 │         ) as bar:
 466 │             for archive in zip_file:
 467 │                 archive.extract()
 468 │                 bar.update(archive.size, archive)
 469 │ 
 470 │     :param iterable: an iterable to iterate over.  If not provided the length
 471 │                      is required.
 472 │     :param length: the number of items to iterate over.  By default the
 473 │                    progressbar will attempt to ask the iterator about its
 474 │                    length, which might or might not work.  If an iterable is
 475 │                    also provided this parameter can be used to override the
 476 │                    length.  If an iterable is not provided the progress bar
 477 │                    will iterate over a range of that length.
 478 │     :param label: the label to show next to the progress bar.
 479 │     :param hidden: hide the progressbar. Defaults to ``False``. When no tty is
 480 │         detected, it will only print the progressbar label. Setting this to
 481 │         ``False`` also disables that.
 482 │     :param show_eta: enables or disables the estimated time display.  This is
 483 │                      automatically disabled if the length cannot be
 484 │                      determined.
 485 │     :param show_percent: enables or disables the percentage display.  The
 486 │                          default is `True` if the iterable has a length or
 487 │                          `False` if not.
 488 │     :param show_pos: enables or disables the absolute position display.  The
 489 │                      default is `False`.
 490 │     :param item_show_func: A function called with the current item which
 491 │         can return a string to show next to the progress bar. If the
 492 │         function returns ``None`` nothing is shown. The current item can
 493 │         be ``None``, such as when entering and exiting the bar.
 494 │     :param fill_char: the character to use to show the filled part of the
 495 │                       progress bar.
 496 │     :param empty_char: the character to use to show the non-filled part of
 497 │                        the progress bar.
 498 │     :param bar_template: the format string to use as template for the bar.
 499 │                          The parameters in it are ``label`` for the label,
 500 │                          ``bar`` for the progress bar and ``info`` for the
 501 │                          info section.
 502 │     :param info_sep: the separator between multiple info items (eta etc.)
 503 │     :param width: the width of the progress bar in characters, 0 means full
 504 │                   terminal width
 505 │     :param file: The file to write to. If this is not a terminal then
 506 │         only the label is printed.
 507 │     :param color: controls if the terminal supports ANSI colors or not.  The
 508 │                   default is autodetection.  This is only needed if ANSI
 509 │                   codes are included anywhere in the progress bar output
 510 │                   which is not the case by default.
 511 │     :param update_min_steps: Render only when this many updates have
 512 │         completed. This allows tuning for very fast iterators.
 513 │ 
 514 │     .. versionadded:: 8.2
 515 │         The ``hidden`` argument.
 516 │ 
 517 │     .. versionchanged:: 8.0
 518 │         Output is shown even if execution time is less than 0.5 seconds.
 519 │ 
 520 │     .. versionchanged:: 8.0
 521 │         ``item_show_func`` shows the current item, not the previous one.
 522 │ 
 523 │     .. versionchanged:: 8.0
 524 │         Labels are echoed if the output is not a TTY. Reverts a change
 525 │         in 7.0 that removed all output.
 526 │ 
 527 │     .. versionadded:: 8.0
 528 │        The ``update_min_steps`` parameter.
 529 │ 
 530 │     .. versionadded:: 4.0
 531 │         The ``color`` parameter and ``update`` method.
 532 │ 
 533 │     .. versionadded:: 2.0
 534 │     """
 535 │     from ._termui_impl import ProgressBar
 536 │ 
 537 │     color = resolve_color_default(color)
 538 │     return ProgressBar(
 539 │         iterable=iterable,
 540 │         length=length,
 541 │         hidden=hidden,
 542 │         show_eta=show_eta,
 543 │         show_percent=show_percent,
 544 │         show_pos=show_pos,
 545 │         item_show_func=item_show_func,
 546 │         fill_char=fill_char,
 547 │         empty_char=empty_char,
 548 │         bar_template=bar_template,
 549 │         info_sep=info_sep,
 550 │         file=file,
 551 │         label=label,
 552 │         width=width,
 553 │         color=color,
 554 │         update_min_steps=update_min_steps,

 572 │ def _interpret_color(color: int | tuple[int, int, int] | str, offset: int = 0) -> str:
 573 │     """Interprets a color value and returns the corresponding ANSI code."""
 574 │     if isinstance(color, str) and color in _ansi_colors:
 575 │         return str(_ansi_colors[color] + offset)
 576 │ 
 577 │     # bool is an int subclass: without the exclusion, True and False would
 578 │     # silently render as the palette indices 1 and 0.
 579 │     elif isinstance(color, int) and not isinstance(color, bool):
 580 │         if 0 <= color <= 255:
 581 │             return f"{38 + offset};5;{color:d}"
 582 │ 
 583 │     elif (
 584 │         isinstance(color, (tuple, list))
 585 │         and len(color) == 3
 586 │         and all(
 587 │             isinstance(c, int) and not isinstance(c, bool) and 0 <= c <= 255
 588 │             for c in color
 589 │         )
 590 │     ):
 591 │         r, g, b = color
 592 │         return f"{38 + offset};2;{r:d};{g:d};{b:d}"
 593 │ 
 594 │     raise ValueError(_("Unknown color {colour!r}").format(colour=color))

 597 │ def style(
 598 │     text: t.Any,
 599 │     fg: int | tuple[int, int, int] | str | None = None,
 600 │     bg: int | tuple[int, int, int] | str | None = None,
 601 │     bold: bool | None = None,
 602 │     dim: bool | None = None,
 603 │     underline: bool | None = None,
 604 │     overline: bool | None = None,
 605 │     italic: bool | None = None,
 606 │     blink: bool | None = None,
 607 │     reverse: bool | None = None,
 608 │     strikethrough: bool | None = None,
 609 │     reset: bool = True,
 610 │ ) -> str:
 611 │     """Styles a text with ANSI styles and returns the new string.  By
 612 │     default the styling is self contained which means that at the end
 613 │     of the string a reset code is issued.  This can be prevented by
 614 │     passing ``reset=False``.
 615 │ 
 616 │     Examples::
 617 │ 
 618 │         click.echo(click.style('Hello World!', fg='green'))
 619 │         click.echo(click.style('ATTENTION!', blink=True))
 620 │         click.echo(click.style('Some things', reverse=True, fg='cyan'))
 621 │         click.echo(click.style('More colors', fg=(255, 12, 128), bg=117))
 622 │ 
 623 │     Supported color names:
 624 │ 
 625 │     * ``black`` (might be a gray)
 626 │     * ``red``
 627 │     * ``green``
 628 │     * ``yellow`` (might be an orange)
 629 │     * ``blue``
 630 │     * ``magenta``
 631 │     * ``cyan``
 632 │     * ``white`` (might be light gray)
 633 │     * ``bright_black``
 634 │     * ``bright_red``
 635 │     * ``bright_green``
 636 │     * ``bright_yellow``
 637 │     * ``bright_blue``
 638 │     * ``bright_magenta``
 639 │     * ``bright_cyan``
 640 │     * ``bright_white``
 641 │     * ``reset`` (reset the color code only)
 642 │ 
 643 │     If the terminal supports it, color may also be specified as:
 644 │ 
 645 │     -   An integer in the interval [0, 255]. The terminal must support
 646 │         8-bit/256-color mode.
 647 │     -   An RGB tuple of three integers in [0, 255]. The terminal must
 648 │         support 24-bit/true-color mode.
 649 │ 
 650 │     See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_color and
 651 │     https://gist.github.com/XVilka/8346728 for more information.
 652 │ 
 653 │     :param text: the string to style with ansi codes.
 654 │     :param fg: if provided this will become the foreground color.
 655 │     :param bg: if provided this will become the background color.
 656 │     :param bold: if provided this will enable or disable bold mode.
 657 │     :param dim: if provided this will enable or disable dim mode.  This is
 658 │                 badly supported.
 659 │     :param underline: if provided this will enable or disable underline.
 660 │     :param overline: if provided this will enable or disable overline.
 661 │     :param italic: if provided this will enable or disable italic.
 662 │     :param blink: if provided this will enable or disable blinking.
 663 │     :param reverse: if provided this will enable or disable inverse
 664 │                     rendering (foreground becomes background and the
 665 │                     other way round).
 666 │     :param strikethrough: if provided this will enable or disable
 667 │         striking through text.
 668 │     :param reset: by default a reset-all code is added at the end of the
 669 │                   string which means that styles do not carry over.  This
 670 │                   can be disabled to compose styles.
 671 │ 
 672 │     .. versionchanged:: 8.5
 673 │         All invalid color values raise :exc:`ValueError`. 256-color index
 674 │         ``0`` is not ignored
 675 │ 
 676 │     .. versionchanged:: 8.0
 677 │         A non-string ``message`` is converted to a string.
 678 │ 
 679 │     .. versionchanged:: 8.0
 680 │        Added support for 256 and RGB color codes.
 681 │ 
 682 │     .. versionchanged:: 8.0
 683 │         Added the ``strikethrough``, ``italic``, and ``overline``
 684 │         parameters.
 685 │ 
 686 │     .. versionchanged:: 7.0
 687 │         Added support for bright colors.
 688 │ 
 689 │     .. versionadded:: 2.0
 690 │     """
 691 │     if not isinstance(text, str):
 692 │         text = str(text)
 693 │ 
 694 │     bits = []
 695 │ 
 696 │     if fg is not None:
 697 │         bits.append(f"\033[{_interpret_color(fg)}m")
 698 │ 
 699 │     if bg is not None:
 700 │         bits.append(f"\033[{_interpret_color(bg, 10)}m")
 701 │ 
 702 │     if bold is not None:
 703 │         bits.append(f"\033[{1 if bold else 22}m")
 704 │     if dim is not None:
 705 │         bits.append(f"\033[{2 if dim else 22}m")
 706 │     if underline is not None:
 707 │         bits.append(f"\033[{4 if underline else 24}m")
 708 │     if overline is not None:
 709 │         bits.append(f"\033[{53 if overline else 55}m")
 710 │     if italic is not None:
 711 │         bits.append(f"\033[{3 if italic else 23}m")
 712 │     if blink is not None:
 713 │         bits.append(f"\033[{5 if blink else 25}m")
 714 │     if reverse is not None:
 715 │         bits.append(f"\033[{7 if reverse else 27}m")
 716 │     if strikethrough is not None:
 717 │         bits.append(f"\033[{9 if strikethrough else 29}m")
 718 │     bits.append(text)
 719 │     if reset:
 720 │         bits.append(_ansi_reset_all)
 721 │     return "".join(bits)

 211 │     )

 323 │ def echo_via_pager(
 324 │     text_or_generator: cabc.Iterable[str] | t.Callable[[], cabc.Iterable[str]] | str,

 328 │     pager on stdout.

 399 │ def progressbar(
 400 │     iterable: cabc.Iterable[V] | None = None,
 401 │     length: int | None = None,
 402 │     label: str | None = None,
 403 │     hidden: bool = False,
 404 │     show_eta: bool = True,
 405 │     show_percent: bool | None = None,
 406 │     show_pos: bool = False,
 407 │     item_show_func: t.Callable[[V | None], str | None] | None = None,
 408 │     fill_char: str = "#",
 409 │     empty_char: str = "-",
 410 │     bar_template: str = "%(label)s  [%(bar)s]  %(info)s",
 411 │     info_sep: str = "  ",
 412 │     width: int = 36,
 413 │     file: t.TextIO | None = None,
 414 │     color: bool | None = None,
 415 │     update_min_steps: int = 1,
 416 │ ) -> ProgressBar[V]:
 417 │     """This function creates an iterable context manager that can be used
 418 │     to iterate over something while showing a progress bar.  It will
 419 │     either iterate over the `iterable` or `length` items (that are counted
 420 │     up).  While iteration happens, this function will print a rendered
 421 │     progress bar to the given `file` (defaults to stdout) and will attempt
 422 │     to calculate remaining time and more.  By default, this progress bar
 423 │     will not be rendered if the file is not a terminal.
 424 │ 
 425 │     The context manager creates the progress bar.  When the context
 426 │     manager is entered the progress bar is already created.  With every
 427 │     iteration over the progress bar, the iterable passed to the bar is
 428 │     advanced and the bar is updated.  When the context manager exits,
 429 │     a newline is printed and the progress bar is finalized on screen.
 430 │ 
 431 │     Note: The progress bar is currently designed for use cases where the
 432 │     total progress can be expected to take at least several seconds.
 433 │     Because of this, the ProgressBar class object won't display
 434 │     progress that is considered too fast, and progress where the time
 435 │     between steps is less than a second.
 436 │ 
 437 │     No printing must happen or the progress bar will be unintentionally
 438 │     destroyed.
 439 │ 
 440 │     Example usage::
 441 │ 
 442 │         with progressbar(items) as bar:
 443 │             for item in bar:
 444 │                 do_something_with(item)
 445 │ 
 446 │     Alternatively, if no iterable is specified, one can manually update the
 447 │     progress bar through the `update()` method instead of directly
 448 │     iterating over the progress bar.  The update method accepts the number
 449 │     of steps to increment the bar with::
 450 │ 
 451 │         with progressbar(length=chunks.total_bytes) as bar:
 452 │             for chunk in chunks:
 453 │                 process_chunk(chunk)
 454 │                 bar.update(chunks.bytes)
 455 │ 
 456 │     The ``update()`` method also takes an optional value specifying the
 457 │     ``current_item`` at the new position. This is useful when used
 458 │     together with ``item_show_func`` to customize the output for each
 459 │     manual step::
 460 │ 
 461 │         with click.progressbar(
 462 │             length=total_size,
 463 │             label='Unzipping archive',
 464 │             item_show_func=lambda a: a.filename
 465 │         ) as bar:
 466 │             for archive in zip_file:
 467 │                 archive.extract()
 468 │                 bar.update(archive.size, archive)
 469 │ 
 470 │     :param iterable: an iterable to iterate over.  If not provided the length
 471 │                      is required.
 472 │     :param length: the number of items to iterate over.  By default the
 473 │                    progressbar will attempt to ask the iterator about its
 474 │                    length, which might or might not work.  If an iterable is
 475 │                    also provided this parameter can be used to override the
 476 │                    length.  If an iterable is not provided the progress bar
 477 │                    will iterate over a range of that length.
 478 │     :param label: the label to show next to the progress bar.
 479 │     :param hidden: hide the progressbar. Defaults to ``False``. When no tty is
 480 │         detected, it will only print the progressbar label. Setting this to
 481 │         ``False`` also disables that.
 482 │     :param show_eta: enables or disables the estimated time display.  This is
 483 │                      automatically disabled if the length cannot be
 484 │                      determined.
 485 │     :param show_percent: enables or disables the percentage display.  The
 486 │                          default is `True` if the iterable has a length or
 487 │                          `False` if not.
 488 │     :param show_pos: enables or disables the absolute position display.  The
 489 │                      default is `False`.
 490 │     :param item_show_func: A function called with the current item which
 491 │         can return a string to show next to the progress bar. If the
 492 │         function returns ``None`` nothing is shown. The current item can
 493 │         be ``None``, such as when entering and exiting the bar.
 494 │     :param fill_char: the character to use to show the filled part of the
 495 │                       progress bar.
 496 │     :param empty_char: the character to use to show the non-filled part of
 497 │                        the progress bar.
 498 │     :param bar_template: the format string to use as template for the bar.
 499 │                          The parameters in it are ``label`` for the label,
 500 │                          ``bar`` for the progress bar and ``info`` for the
 501 │                          info section.
 502 │     :param info_sep: the separator between multiple info items (eta etc.)
 503 │     :param width: the width of the progress bar in characters, 0 means full
 504 │                   terminal width
 505 │     :param file: The file to write to. If this is not a terminal then
 506 │         only the label is printed.
 507 │     :param color: controls if the terminal supports ANSI colors or not.  The
 508 │                   default is autodetection.  This is only needed if ANSI
 509 │                   codes are included anywhere in the progress bar output
 510 │                   which is not the case by default.
 511 │     :param update_min_steps: Render only when this many updates have
 512 │         completed. This allows tuning for very fast iterators.
 513 │ 
 514 │     .. versionadded:: 8.2
 515 │         The ``hidden`` argument.
 516 │ 
 517 │     .. versionchanged:: 8.0
 518 │         Output is shown even if execution time is less than 0.5 seconds.
 519 │ 
 520 │     .. versionchanged:: 8.0
 521 │         ``item_show_func`` shows the current item, not the previous one.
 522 │ 
 523 │     .. versionchanged:: 8.0
 524 │         Labels are echoed if the output is not a TTY. Reverts a change
 525 │         in 7.0 that removed all output.
 526 │ 
 527 │     .. versionadded:: 8.0
 528 │        The ``update_min_steps`` parameter.
 529 │ 
 530 │     .. versionadded:: 4.0
 531 │         The ``color`` parameter and ``update`` method.
 532 │ 
 533 │     .. versionadded:: 2.0
 534 │     """
 535 │     from ._termui_impl import ProgressBar
 536 │ 
 537 │     color = resolve_color_default(color)
 538 │     return ProgressBar(
 539 │         iterable=iterable,
 540 │         length=length,
 541 │         hidden=hidden,
 542 │         show_eta=show_eta,
 543 │         show_percent=show_percent,
 544 │         show_pos=show_pos,
 545 │         item_show_func=item_show_func,
 546 │         fill_char=fill_char,
 547 │         empty_char=empty_char,
 548 │         bar_template=bar_template,
 549 │         info_sep=info_sep,
 550 │         file=file,
 551 │         label=label,
 552 │         width=width,
 553 │         color=color,
 554 │         update_min_steps=update_min_steps,
 555 │     )

 572 │ def _interpret_color(color: int | tuple[int, int, int] | str, offset: int = 0) -> str:
 573 │     """Interprets a color value and returns the corresponding ANSI code."""
 574 │     if isinstance(color, str) and color in _ansi_colors:
 575 │         return str(_ansi_colors[color] + offset)
 576 │ 
 577 │     # bool is an int subclass: without the exclusion, True and False would
 578 │     # silently render as the palette indices 1 and 0.
 579 │     elif isinstance(color, int) and not isinstance(color, bool):
 580 │         if 0 <= color <= 255:
 581 │             return f"{38 + offset};5;{color:d}"
 582 │ 
 583 │     elif (
 584 │         isinstance(color, (tuple, list))
 585 │         and len(color) == 3
 586 │         and all(
 587 │             isinstance(c, int) and not isinstance(c, bool) and 0 <= c <= 255
 588 │             for c in color
 589 │         )
 590 │     ):
 591 │         r, g, b = color
 592 │         return f"{38 + offset};2;{r:d};{g:d};{b:d}"
 593 │ 
 594 │     raise ValueError(_("Unknown color {colour!r}").format(colour=color))

 597 │ def style(
 598 │     text: t.Any,
 599 │     fg: int | tuple[int, int, int] | str | None = None,
 600 │     bg: int | tuple[int, int, int] | str | None = None,
 601 │     bold: bool | None = None,

 605 │     italic: bool | None = None,
 606 │     blink: bool | None = None,
 607 │     reverse: bool | None = None,
 608 │     strikethrough: bool | None = None,
 609 │     reset: bool = True,
 610 │ ) -> str:
 611 │     """Styles a text with ANSI styles and returns the new string.  By
 612 │     default the styling is self contained which means that at the end
 613 │     of the string a reset code is issued.  This can be prevented by
 614 │     passing ``reset=False``.
 615 │ 
 616 │     Examples::
 617 │ 
 618 │         click.echo(click.style('Hello World!', fg='green'))
 619 │         click.echo(click.style('ATTENTION!', blink=True))
 620 │         click.echo(click.style('Some things', reverse=True, fg='cyan'))
 621 │         click.echo(click.style('More colors', fg=(255, 12, 128), bg=117))
 622 │ 
 623 │     Supported color names:
 624 │ 
 625 │     * ``black`` (might be a gray)
 626 │     * ``red``
 627 │     * ``green``
 628 │     * ``yellow`` (might be an orange)
 629 │     * ``blue``
 630 │     * ``magenta``
 631 │     * ``cyan``
 632 │     * ``white`` (might be light gray)
 633 │     * ``bright_black``
 634 │     * ``bright_red``
 635 │     * ``bright_green``
 636 │     * ``bright_yellow``
 637 │     * ``bright_blue``
 638 │     * ``bright_magenta``
 639 │     * ``bright_cyan``
 640 │     * ``bright_white``
 641 │     * ``reset`` (reset the color code only)
 642 │ 
 643 │     If the terminal supports it, color may also be specified as:
 644 │ 
 645 │     -   An integer in the interval [0, 255]. The terminal must support
 646 │         8-bit/256-color mode.
 647 │     -   An RGB tuple of three integers in [0, 255]. The terminal must
 648 │         support 24-bit/true-color mode.
 649 │ 
 650 │     See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_color and
 651 │     https://gist.github.com/XVilka/8346728 for more information.
 652 │ 
 653 │     :param text: the string to style with ansi codes.
 654 │     :param fg: if provided this will become the foreground color.
 655 │     :param bg: if provided this will become the background color.
 656 │     :param bold: if provided this will enable or disable bold mode.
 657 │     :param dim: if provided this will enable or disable dim mode.  This is
 658 │                 badly supported.
 659 │     :param underline: if provided this will enable or disable underline.
 660 │     :param overline: if provided this will enable or disable overline.
 661 │     :param italic: if provided this will enable or disable italic.
 662 │     :param blink: if provided this will enable or disable blinking.
 663 │     :param reverse: if provided this will enable or disable inverse
 664 │                     rendering (foreground becomes background and the
 665 │                     other way round).
 666 │     :param strikethrough: if provided this will enable or disable
 667 │         striking through text.
 668 │     :param reset: by default a reset-all code is added at the end of the
 669 │                   string which means that styles do not carry over.  This
 670 │                   can be disabled to compose styles.
 671 │ 
 672 │     .. versionchanged:: 8.5
 673 │         All invalid color values raise :exc:`ValueError`. 256-color index
 674 │         ``0`` is not ignored
 675 │ 
 676 │     .. versionchanged:: 8.0
 677 │         A non-string ``message`` is converted to a string.
 678 │ 
 679 │     .. versionchanged:: 8.0
 680 │        Added support for 256 and RGB color codes.
 681 │ 
 682 │     .. versionchanged:: 8.0
 683 │         Added the ``strikethrough``, ``italic``, and ``overline``
 684 │         parameters.
 685 │ 
 686 │     .. versionchanged:: 7.0
 687 │         Added support for bright colors.
 688 │ 
 689 │     .. versionadded:: 2.0
 690 │     """
 691 │     if not isinstance(text, str):
 692 │         text = str(text)
 693 │ 
 694 │     bits = []
 695 │ 
 696 │     if fg is not None:
 697 │         bits.append(f"\033[{_interpret_color(fg)}m")
 698 │ 
 699 │     if bg is not None:
 700 │         bits.append(f"\033[{_interpret_color(bg, 10)}m")
 701 │ 
 702 │     if bold is not None:
 703 │         bits.append(f"\033[{1 if bold else 22}m")
 704 │     if dim is not None:
 705 │         bits.append(f"\033[{2 if dim else 22}m")
 706 │     if underline is not None:
 707 │         bits.append(f"\033[{4 if underline else 24}m")
 708 │     if overline is not None:
 709 │         bits.append(f"\033[{53 if overline else 55}m")
 710 │     if italic is not None:

 712 │     if blink is not None:
 713 │         bits.append(f"\033[{5 if blink else 25}m")
 714 │     if reverse is not None:
 715 │         bits.append(f"\033[{7 if reverse else 27}m")
 716 │     if strikethrough is not None:
 717 │         bits.append(f"\033[{9 if strikethrough else 29}m")
 718 │     bits.append(text)
 719 │     if reset:
 720 │         bits.append(_ansi_reset_all)
